definitions.note: a noun phrase: the headgear itself, as opposed to the bit it holds

blocks.note: first meaning: to draw oneself up in anger or offence
second meaning: the harness on a horse's head, which holds the mouthpiece but is not that mouthpiece

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a bit!' reads as an emphatic denial ('not at all'), but literally it says this item of tack is not the bit itself, only the straps that carry it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to take offence visibly, and a bridle is the set of straps a rider uses to steer a horse.

definitions.note: past tense in the clue, while the answer is the plain verb

indicators.note: done casually means done carelessly, without keeping things in their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone strolled across without any hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The tense is loose: 'wandered' would strictly want ROVED, but the four letters of 'over' give only the plain verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rove is to roam about aimlessly from place to place, a close synonym of wandering.

clue.text: Yet such things don't cost the earth

definitions.text: Yet such things don't cost the earth

blocks.clueFragment: Yet such things don't cost the earth
blocks.note: surface reading: bargains that are not expensive
setter's reading: earth is soil, so the paradox is that these things are named after soil yet do not cost it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Yet' points to the paradox: the phrase for a bargain contains a word for earth, while 'not costing the earth' is the idiom for being cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt-cheap means extremely inexpensive, exactly what is meant by not costing the earth.

blocks.note: first meaning: the second book of the Old Testament
second meaning: a mass departure or escape of people

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests reserving a seat on a plane; 'Book' is a noun, a biblical title, and 'flight' means fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's second book tells of the Israelites leaving Egypt, and the word now means any large-scale departure of people.

clue.text: Catalogue banned at the last minute

blocks.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, forbidden
arriving at the last minute is arriving late

explanation.surface: A catalogue was withdrawn just before it was due to be published.
explanation.definitionFit: To catalogue something is to list it systematically, and to tabulate is to set data out in a table.

clue.text: Reveal what offers kept a reserve

indicators.note: read as re-serve, to serve up again, so the letters before it are dished out a second time in a new arrangement

blocks.note: all fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An auction lot is unveiled to show which bids held a reserve price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like an auction's minimum price, but split as re-serve it signals the rearrangement of the fifteen letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the wraps off something is to unveil it publicly for the first time, an idiom for revealing.

blocks.note: a bill is a banknote, especially in American usage
in a hook-and-eye fastening, the hook is the part that catches the eye

explanation.surface: Pay attention to an eye-catching garden tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye-catching' seems to mean striking, but it describes the part of a clothes fastener that catches the little loop called the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A billhook is a heavy curved-bladed tool used for cutting back branches and hedges.

indicators.note: the word for ringing goes around the single letter, its letters on either side
in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside CALL to make CALIL, which read upwards gives LILAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a flowering bush with fragrant purple or white blossom, so a type of shrub.

clue.text: Soldering irons start making electronic device

indicators.note: soldering joins parts together into something new, so these letters are fused into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An electronics hobbyist heats soldering irons to assemble a component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldering irons' reads as one tool, but 'Soldering' is the signal and 'irons start' the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A transistor is a semiconductor component that amplifies or switches current in circuits.

blocks.note: first meaning: to fail to notice or to ignore
second meaning: to supervise or oversee

explanation.surface: Someone has lost the knack of leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are nearly opposite: missing something and watching over it.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook can mean to fail to see or neglect, and also to oversee or watch over from above.

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so the letters are laid out in another way

blocks.note: taken as written
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a typical Scotsman's name

explanation.surface: A young woman takes against a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-disposed' looks like one word meaning hostile; split, it is the fodder and its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilian is a female given name, and crosswords often define names simply by the sex of their bearers.

blocks.note: surface reading: a judge summarising the accusation in court
setter's reading: literally tally the price, which is also the idiom for weighing up the drawbacks of an action

explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom picture of a judge summing up is a decoy; read literally, it is adding up a price, and the phrase for that means assessing the consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: To count the cost is to reckon up the expense, or figuratively to weigh the damage or risk of a course of action.

clue.text: It's sad, but courage is needed as a policeman

blocks.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: A melancholy officer must summon up courage to do the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Bluebottle is old British slang for a police officer, from the blue uniform; it is also a large fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle was a nineteenth-century slang term for a constable, after the dark blue uniform.

blocks.note: first meaning: a colour
second meaning: low in spirits

explanation.walkthrough: 'A shade depressed' reads as 'slightly down', but 'A shade' is a colour on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is a colour of the spectrum, and feeling blue is an idiom for being sad or low.

clue.text: You're out of spirits when he leaves

definitions.text: You're out of spirits when he leaves

blocks.clueFragment: You're out of spirits when he leaves
blocks.note: surface reading: the bar is dry once a particular person has gone
setter's reading: spirits are ghosts or demons, cast out by a priestly visitor

explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of spirits' suggests no gin left or low morale; the spirits are demons, and the man who leaves has driven them out.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorcist is someone, often a priest, who expels evil spirits from a person or place.

blocks.note: first meaning: grasps an idea
second meaning: becomes fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone who grasps things quickly becomes well liked.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to grasp something eventually and to become popular or widely adopted.

indicators.note: the extremities of a word are its two ends, and these are dropped
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a puppet worked by strings, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a string puppet, breaking off its hands and feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first and last letters of 'marionette' to leave ARIONETT, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear into someone is to assault or criticise them fiercely, an idiom for attacking.

blocks.note: surface reading: the romantic season of spring
setter's reading: spring means jump, and tradition lets women propose marriage on 29 February of the extra-day year

explanation.walkthrough: 'Springtime' suggests the season; read as a jumping time it points to the year with an extra day, when by old custom a woman may propose to a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Every fourth year February has a twenty-ninth day, and folklore allows women to make the marriage proposal then.

clue.text: Go for a jog, taking wrong turn

indicators.note: taking a turn means a change of course, so the letters change their order

blocks.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A runner goes out jogging and takes a wrong turning.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is the legal term for a civil wrong, such as negligence.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot is to run at a gentle, steady pace, much like jogging.

definitions.note: a noun, where the answer as written is usually a verb; a step-up is a rise in rank

blocks.note: first meaning: increase the pace
second meaning: a rise to a higher position

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests fast-tracking someone's career; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up is to speed up or intensify, and a step up is an advance to a better job or rank.

clue.text: The key to a high state of readiness?

blocks.note: first meaning: the standard tuning for orchestral instruments
second meaning: being fully prepared and keyed up

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'the secret of being ready', but 'key' is musical: concert pitch is a standard tuning, a little higher than older pitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Concert pitch is the internationally agreed tuning for instruments, and figuratively a state of keen preparedness.

blocks.note: first meaning: to decorate metal by cutting or embossing
second meaning: a pursuit of game, or the open ground it takes place on

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests etching a picture of a hunt onto metal; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasing is the craft of decorating metal by engraving, and a chase is a hunt or a tract of hunting land.

clue.text: A case of pin and needles

definitions.text: A case of pin and needles

blocks.clueFragment: A case of pin and needles
blocks.note: surface reading: an instance of the tingling feeling in a numb limb
setter's reading: a case is a container, here a small one for sewing pins and needles

explanation.walkthrough: 'A case of pins and needles' sounds medical; the case is a small box that holds sewing kit.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for holding needles, pins and other small sewing tools.

blocks.note: first meaning: to exert oneself hard
second meaning: a breed or stock of animals or plants

explanation.surface: An athlete pushes hard in a running contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' reads as a contest, but it means a breed or lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain is to exert oneself to the limit, and a strain is a particular breed, variety or bloodline.

clue.text: It comes in to fight on the other side

indicators.note: something that comes in enters, so this word goes inside the other one

blocks.note: to oppose is to fight against
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone joins a battle on the enemy's side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes in to fight' reads as joining a battle; here 'It' is the piece that enters the word for fighting against.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite can mean facing or across from, that is, situated on the far side.

clue.text: We are shortly getting a pack animal of legendary reputation

definitions.text: a pack animal of legendary reputation

blocks.note: we're is the shortened form of we are, written without its apostrophe
wolves hunt in packs

explanation.surface: We are soon to acquire a beast of burden with a famous name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack animal' suggests a mule carrying loads, but it is an animal that hunts in a pack; the whole phrase with 'of legendary reputation' also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A werewolf is a mythical person who turns into a wolf, a creature of folklore and legend.

blocks.note: surface reading: a competitor in front from start to finish
setter's reading: lead is the graphite core of a writing implement, running its whole length

explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds the lead' sounds like a race leader; the lead is the graphite core, held along the full length of the wooden stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil is a wooden writing instrument with a graphite core, traditionally called its lead, running through it.
